summary.headline: The Advisory Committee voted to recommend water connections near the Parkerville landfill and finalized its report for Special Town Meeting.
summary.summary: The Advisory Committee voted unanimously to recommend Article 7, which funds $240,000 for town water main extensions and connections for two homes impacted by the Parkerville Road landfill. Members conducted a detailed line-by-line review and edit of their draft report and recommendations for the October 17 Special Town Meeting warrant articles, including articles on two-family zoning, golf course irrigation, trail bridges, and a stormwater enterprise fund. The committee voted to adopt the finalized report with minor editorial discretion granted to the chair, and reviewed upcoming meeting scheduling regarding the Neary School building project.

topics.title: Article 7: Water connection for two homes near Parkerville landfill
topics.summary: The committee revisited Article 7, which requests $240,000 from water retained earnings to extend the town water main and connect two homes near the closed Parkerville Road landfill. The chair confirmed with the Select Board chair that the town will cover the full cost of the connection from the street to the houses, as the connection was necessitated by landfill-related testing issues. Following this clarification, the committee voted unanimously to recommend the article.
key_details: Connects two homes on Parkerville Road impacted by proximity to the landfill.
The town will pay the entire connection cost from the street main into the private homes.
Voted 6-0 to recommend approval as printed in the warrant.
topics.why_it_matters: Authorizes $240,000 in town water funds to address drinking water concerns near the town landfill and clarifies that property owners will not bear the hookup costs.

topics.title: Review and editing of Advisory Committee Special Town Meeting report
topics.summary: The committee performed a comprehensive text review and revision of its draft report and recommendations for the October 17 Special Town Meeting warrant articles. Key adjustments clarified financial details on personal property tax exemptions under Article 8, clarified that Article 6 rescinds unissued borrowing authority rather than returning cash, explained the function and lack of immediate fees for the Article 5 stormwater enterprise fund, and refined explanations on trail bridge costs, golf course irrigation funding, and concerns regarding two-family zoning under Article 2. At the conclusion of the review, the committee voted to approve the report as amended.
key_details: Article 8 clarification: Raising exemption to $2,500 exempts 22 accounts with a total assessed value of $40,100.
Article 6 clarification: Rescinding remaining authorized borrowing of $727,960 for Breakneck Hill and $375,000 for the Neary School study because projects required less debt than authorized.
Article 5 clarification: Establishes the enterprise fund as an accounting structure only; no stormwater fees are created without future Town Meeting authorization.
Article 4 and 3 refinements: Adjusted phrasing on high trail bridge costs per linear foot and noted taxpayer funding concerns versus self-sustaining operations at the golf course.
Article 2 zoning: Retained explanation of committee concerns regarding removal of the two-year ownership requirement and potential neighborhood character impacts.
topics.why_it_matters: The Advisory Committee report provides official voter guidance and cost analyses for all warrant articles presented at Special Town Meeting.

topics.title: Future meeting schedule and Neary School project update
topics.summary: The committee reviewed its calendar ahead of the October 17 Special Town Meeting. Members discussed a tentative request from the School Building Committee, superintendent, and Select Board for a joint meeting on October 13 to review five architectural options and preliminary cost ranges for the Neary School building project. Members agreed not to hold a standalone meeting on October 13 if the joint meeting is not finalized, and decided against holding a pre-meeting immediately before Town Meeting on October 17.
key_details: Special Town Meeting is scheduled for October 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM at Trottier Middle School.
Joint meeting regarding Neary School building options tentatively discussed for October 13 at 6:30 PM, subject to final confirmation.
The committee opted not to hold a separate meeting on October 13 if the joint session does not occur.
topics.why_it_matters: Sets committee attendance and potential review of options for the major upcoming Neary School building project.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee reviewed and voted to approve three sets of past meeting minutes and adjourned.
key_details: Approved minutes of August 5, 2026 (5-0-1, with one abstention).
Approved minutes of the August 11, 2026 joint meeting with the Select Board (4-0-2, with two abstentions).

Approve the Advisory Committee report for Special Town Meeting as edited, authorizing the chair or drafter to make minor edits and formatting corrections
